main_body: A wooden treasure chest with iron straps and a keyhole lock, heaped with gold coins and gems above the rim. A small loose gold pile sits at the bottom right.
top_band: Gold and gem heap at rows 3-8 (light gold L~138 at rows 7-8, gems and highlights above). It is separated from the wood front (L~101, from row 9) by a step of about 37 L.
evidence: The column at x=17 reads as a gold heap surface (rows 3-8), then the wooden front face (rows 9-15) with straps, a dark band at row 12 and a lock. The heap surface seen from above counts as the container contents, so the projection is a valid 3/4 view. The kind is wrong: the main body is a standing chest with a gold heap, not scattered floor debris such as bones, rubble or shards, so the kind label does not describe it. The verdict is fail on that mismatch alone; the geometry itself would pass.

style.evidence: The candidate has 27 distinct colours per tile against 17-20 for the references. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, and the dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines are tinted dark brown. Wood has several steps (light, mid, dark, deep), and the gold heap has highlights, gems and shaded coins. It is at least as rich as the stall and well references and does not look sticker-like.
